clue.text: Mail quiet individual is to pigeon-hole

parts.note: to mail a letter is to post it
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a single individual is one

explanation.surface: A postal worker is told off to sort letters into the right slots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pigeon-hole' looks like the sorting rack in a post office, but as a verb it means to shelve something for later.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeon-hole a plan is to set it aside and defer it to a later time.

clue.text: Sponsor two small boys

parts.note: Pat is a shortened form of the boy's name Patrick
Ron is a shortened form of the boy's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A backer supports two little lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' means the names are shortened: Pat and Ron.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron gives financial support, as a sponsor or benefactor does.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to maroon someone is to leave them stuck, abandoned

explanation.surface: A thread in a dark reddish colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maroon' looks like the colour, but it is the verb for leaving someone stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone stranded is to maroon them, and a single fibre twisted into rope is called a strand.

clue.text: Objections against or in favour of trials

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
tests are trials

explanation.surface: People argue against or for some trials.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets 'against' against 'in favour of', but 'against' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Objections raised against something are complaints or demonstrations of dissent.

clue.text: Fine stallion carrying one home

indicators.note: carrying means the words Fine stallion hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A good horse carries someone home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is its home, and the word also means a cosy place to live.

clue.text: Raved about key part of speech

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word raved are moved around into a new order

parts.note: B is one of the musical keys, named by a letter

explanation.surface: Someone ranted about a crucial grammatical category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RAVED into ADVER, and the key B finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar lists the adverb among the word classes, alongside noun, verb and adjective.

clue.text: Specify dock

definitions.meaning: to dock an animal is to cut off its tail

explanation.surface: Someone names a dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour, but it means cutting off a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to list point by point; to de-tail is to dock, removing the tail.

clue.text: Removes passages

definitions.meaning: short pieces of text taken from a longer work

explanation.surface: Someone cuts out pieces of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pulls out; as a noun it means quoted excerpts from a text.

clue.text: He has a part to play, rising in support of the composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, support of means the second piece sits underneath the first

parts.note: J S Bach was a German composer

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a role is a part to play in a drama

explanation.surface: An actor's part climbs to prop up the composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ROLE into ELOR, and 'in support of' puts it under BACH in this down clue. 'He' is the definition: such a person is male.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is a bachelor, so the word always refers to a male.

clue.text: Expected to be slow — so it tore around!

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of the words so it tore are turned about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Nobody thought this creature would be quick, so its frantic dash is a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' shuffles the eight letters of SO IT TORE; the surface recalls the fable of the hare and the slow, steady winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled reptile is proverbially sluggish, famous for its plodding pace.

clue.text: Stable mousers holding it back

indicators.note: back signals that the whole assembled run is read in the reverse direction
holding means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: cats are kept as mousers, catching mice

explanation.surface: Cats in the stable are keeping hold of something and pulling it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'back' together give CITATS turned round. 'Stable' looks like a horse's building, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is unchanging and motionless, without fluctuation.

clue.text: Stuff with hair perhaps, as a security measure

parts.note: to pad is to stuff or fill out
a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: Someone fills a pillow with hair for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shows LOCK is an example of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable lock on a hasp or chain keeps things secure.

clue.text: Animals in the pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard is also called the ounce, so these are big cats
there are sixteen of these weight units in one pound avoirdupois

explanation.surface: Stray animals are held in the local pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests an enclosure for strays, but it is the unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow leopards are known as ounces, and the small weight unit is a sixteenth part of a pound.

clue.text: It's no good when old, to go in for chaff

parts.note: something no good is bad
to go in is to be inside, so the word in itself supplies these letters
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone says bad things only get worse with age before swapping them for husks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' looks like grain husks, but it means teasing banter here; the pieces are taken in answer order, not clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a noun is teasing talk, playful banter between friends.

clue.text: Struggles to get right inside Cornish resort

indicators.note: inside means one letter is placed within the resort's name

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: Someone battles to reach the right place in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: ST IVES is a seaside town in Cornwall, the county at the south-western tip of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strives makes great efforts, battling hard.

clue.text: August, when one finds holy man at cathedral site

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
Ely is an English city with a famous cathedral

explanation.surface: In August, a saint turns up at a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month, but as an adjective it means dignified. ELY is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something grand, dignified and imposing in manner.

clue.text: A man needed to ring tuberculin-tested duck

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
TT stands for tuberculin-tested, as on milk labels
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A man is needed to put a ring on a duck that has been tested for tuberculosis.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a nought in cricket, O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: High-handed to notice crooked dice pocketed

indicators.note: pocketed means one piece is tucked inside the other
crooked dice are loaded or bent, so the letters of dice are rearranged

parts.note: to spot is to notice

explanation.surface: A cheat is caught out when the loaded dice are slipped into a pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' turns the dice letters into DEIC, and 'pocketed' tucks the noticing word inside, so the dice surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules absolutely, so a tyrannical manner is overbearing and imperious.

clue.text: Bruised apple you're lucky to get

definitions.meaning: fruit knocked from a tree by the wind, often bruised
an unexpected gain or stroke of luck

explanation.surface: Fallen fruit is a lucky find.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit blown off a tree has that name, and so does an unexpected bonus or sudden gain.

clue.text: Advocated dope's use — disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously signals that the letters of dope's use are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone recommended drug use, with terrible results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrously' rearranges DOPES and USE. 'Advocated' is a verb in the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to support or champion it.

clue.text: Censor can do what Canute could not

parts.words: can do what Canute could not
parts.note: King Canute failed to turn back the tide; spelling the word tide backwards gives this verb

explanation.surface: A censor has powers that even King Canute lacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says King Canute could not turn back the tide; written backwards, TIDE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor cuts and revises material before it is published.

clue.text: See — the broken ice does

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of ice does are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone sees ice cracking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ICE DOES. 'See' looks like a verb, but a see is a bishop's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under that bishop's authority.

clue.text: Supporter of something that must be cracked

definitions.text: Supporter of something that must be cracked

parts.words: Supporter of something that must be cracked
parts.note: the thing to be cracked is a breakfast item with a shell, and the holder props it up

explanation.surface: Someone supports a problem that has to be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' suggests a code or puzzle, but it is a boiled breakfast item held upright in its cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holds a boiled one upright so its shell can be broken at the table.

clue.text: A gin's uplifting in an austere place

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap, here plural

explanation.surface: A gin brings cheer in a bleak place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses A + TRAPS upwards. 'gin' looks like the spirit, but it is a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city-state was famous for its harsh, frugal discipline.

clue.text: Present sly student dropped, with refusal to conform

parts.note: to be present is to be here

indicators.note: dropped means a letter is removed from the word sly

parts.note: L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A sneaky student is expelled for refusing to toe the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes L (learner) from SLY, leaving SY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief that departs from accepted doctrine.

clue.text: Descent, partially roped, from Eiger — tricky!

indicators.note: partially means only some of the letters of the word roped are used
tricky signals that the letters of Eiger are juggled into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber comes down the Eiger on a rope, a hard climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes PED from roped and 'tricky' turns EIGER into IGREE. The surface is about climbing down, but 'Descent' means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent can mean family line, and a pedigree is a recorded ancestry.

clue.text: Unite the pair

definitions.meaning: to unite is to join or link together
a pair of people or things, two together

explanation.surface: Two people are joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means join or link; as a noun it means two partners or items.

clue.text: List books the painter holds

indicators.note: holds means the painter's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An artist owns a list of books.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Academician) and OT (Old Testament) are crossword conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a roster, a schedule of who does what and when.

clue.text: Abstraction of ten — car breakdown

indicators.note: a breakdown smashes the letters of ten and car apart to be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ten cars break down and someone looks absent-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' rearranges TEN and CAR. 'Abstraction' here means being lost in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstraction can mean absent-mindedness, a dreamy state like being in a daze.

clue.text: Studies precise way to interpret

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
true can mean exact or accurate, as in a true line

explanation.surface: A student pores over books to find the exact way to read a text.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an old usage that crosswords use a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a text is to work out or explain its meaning.

clue.text: Briefly, state hip replacement's needed for the sultan

parts.note: CAL is a short form of California, a US state

indicators.note: replacement signals that the letters of hip are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: In short, a ruler needs a new hip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges HIP into IPH.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was a Muslim ruler, and a sultan is a similar Islamic sovereign.

clue.text: Letter from country-woman

parts.note: a land is a country or nation
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a woman in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a written message, but it means someone who lets out rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets property to tenants is a letter in this sense.
